Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Herrera (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Noah Grant (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Bayridge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive financial workloads, wants reserved GPUs, strict isolation, burst capacity for periodic peaks, and audit/KMS controls. Next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark.

Topics: dedicated capacity sizing, isolation & VPC/on-prem options, burst strategy (burst pools / autoscale), SLAs, benchmarking, security (SOC2/ISO, KMS), timeline and POC scope.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do intros quick. I'm Maya Chen, AE. Alex here is our SE.
[00:08] Sam (Bayridge CTO): Hey thanks, Sam Patel. We're excited to hear how Redwood might fit our inference needs. We've been talking about dedicated capacity — low latency for trading models.
[00:18] Lena (Head of ML): Lena here, we run a couple of transformer models for risk scoring and a latency sensitive fraud model, mostly 1k token windows, sometimes 2k.
[00:28] Alex (Redwood SE): Got it. Quick qual question — current infra and traffic shape? average qps, burst patterns?
[00:34] Noah (Infra): We have around 120 rps avg across the models during day, spikes to 600 rps for market open/close windows, those spikes last 10-20 minutes. We can't tolerate >150ms p50 for the fraud model.
[00:48] Maya: Thanks. And what's your current stack — cloud provider, any on-prem constraints, SSO/KMS?
[00:54] Priya (Security): We're on AWS, private subnets, strict VPC peering rules, we use AWS KMS with custom CMKs. SOC 2 Type II in place, ISO on roadmap.
[01:06] Alex: Perfect. So Dedicated would give you reserved GPU pools — isolation and configurable autoscale. For the burst you mentioned, we can do reserved baseline plus burst capacity on-demand or via a shared burst pool.
[01:20] Sam: How does billing work for burst? We don't want to pay for idle reserved nodes but need guarantees for the spikes.
[01:26] Maya: Primary model is reserved (monthly commit) for baseline throughput, and you can configure burst policies to allow short-term capacity from host pool billed at higher rate. We can design a hybrid — smaller reserve + burst for peaks.
[01:38] Lena: For the models — quantization is an option right? we care about accuracy. Are you recommending int8?
[01:44] Alex: Yeah we typically recommend mixed approach — int8/4 quant for non-critical models, and for the fraud model we might keep fp16 or use int8 with evals. We do model profiling and provide quantization recommendation per workload.
[01:57] Noah: What about the KV cache and prefetched prompts — do you persist cache between requests? we saw notes about KV cache on your docs but need clarity on isolation.
[02:06] Alex: We use per-tenant KV cache within the dedicated runtime; it's isolated to your pool. There's an auto-prefix cache that reduces token compute for repeated context, but we can disable if you want strict statelessness.
[02:18] Priya: Important: audit logs and key access — we need HSM/KMS integration and full audit trail for tokens and request metadata. Also data residency — some logs must stay in us-east-1.
[02:29] Maya: We support customer KMS integration and can map key usage. Audit logs are available in the console with retention options; we'll share the SOC2/ISO checklist and network architecture doc.
[02:38] Sam: Performance — any published numbers for A100? what's typical token latency at our 1k window?
[02:45] Alex: For A100 with optimized kernels, typical p50 for 1k tokens is 90-140ms depending on batching. For low-latency workloads we can tune batch sizes and disable long batching. We'll run a benchmark with your model to be precise.
[02:57] Lena: Ok, we also have a model variant that uses 2.7B param for some scoring, and a larger 13B for deeper analytics. Would you recommend colocating them in same pool?
[03:08] Alex: Ideally separate pools per model family for better isolation and scheduling. You can have a high-priority pool for the fraud model (lower latency SLO) and a cheaper pool for the 13B analytics. Routing policies can fallback to hosted if dedicated is saturated.
[03:21] Noah: How fast is autoscale — can we guarantee capacity increase in under a minute during spikes?
[03:27] Alex: Autoscale react time depends on pre-warmed instances and available capacity. For guaranteed sub-minute scale we'd recommend pre-provisioned burst capacity (warm instances) or keeping a small buffer in the reserved pool. On Dedicated we can configure warm pool policies.
[03:40] Priya: Security question — can we run in our VPC or is it managed by Redwood?
[03:44] Maya: Both options exist. Private deployment gives you control over the control plane, or we offer VPC peering and PrivateLink for Dedicated with strict network controls. For regulated stuff, many customers choose Private or VPC-attached Dedicated.
[03:56] Sam: If we go Private (on-prem variant), what's the typical installation timeline?
[04:00] Alex: On-prem takes longer — typical project is 8-12 weeks for deployment and validation, depending on your infra. VPC-connected dedicated is much faster, usually 2-4 weeks.
[04:10] Lena: We care about model rollouts and A/B tests. Does Redwood support canary rollouts?
[04:14] Maya: Yes — canary, traffic shaping, and automatic fallback to host models if deployment fails. Console gives per-route dashboards and tracing hooks.
[04:23] Sam: SLA and uptime?
[04:25] Maya: Dedicated includes SLA options; we can propose latency/uptime targets in the SOW.
[04:29] Noah: Any limits on number of models or concurrent sessions?
[04:33] Alex: Not strict limits — depends on pool size. We'll size based on concurrency & qps. We'll need your traffic histogram to propose a pool configuration.
[04:43] Priya: Compliance — can you show us specifics around data encryption in transit at rest, role-based access control?
[04:48] Maya: Yes, we'll share the security pack. We support RBAC and can integrate with your SSO/SAML.
[04:54] Lena: On benchmarking — we'll want a 2-week window with our request traces and synthetic load. What does Redwood need?
[04:59] Alex: We'll need a sample trace, model repo or weights, and expected latency SLO. We can run a controlled benchmark and provide per-token cost estimates and latency breakdowns.
[05:10] Sam: Pricing is the hard part — send us a few configurations: small baseline reserve + burst, and a full-commit reserved option. Include cost per token estimates.
[05:18] Maya: Absolutely. We'll send a pricing sheet for a 4x A100 baseline with warm burst pool options and an annual commit option.
[05:24] Noah: One more nit — network egress and peering cost assumptions?
[05:28] Maya: We'll include estimated networking costs and region options; most customers colocate to avoid egress.
[05:34] Priya: Also need contract length options and termination clauses for reserved capacity.
[05:38] Maya: We'll include standard and enterprise terms in the SOW.
[05:42] Alex: To summarize technical path: collect traffic profiles, size baseline reserved pool, plan warm burst policy, run 2-week benchmark, and finalize SOW based on results.
[05:52] Sam: That sounds good. Proposed timeline?
[05:55] Maya: We'll send pricing and security docs by 3/6, schedule deep-dive with infra/security on 3/9, and aim to start benchmarks the following week (3/16).
[06:03] Lena: Ok. Qs from my side — does Redwood support deterministic inference for auditability?
[06:09] Alex: We can run deterministic seeds and capture outputs for audit traces; sampling-based models may introduce variance, but we can configure temperature / sampling to be reproducible.
[06:18] Priya: For KMS — we need to ensure keys are customer-managed and not rotated without our control.
[06:23] Maya: Understood. We'll document key management options and integration details.
[06:28] Sam: Any references or customer success stories in finance?
[06:31] Maya: We can share redacted case studies — e.g., a trading desk that moved to dedicated for low-latency inference and reduced per-token cost by 30% while meeting latency SLOs.
[06:40] Noah: Ok thanks. Nothing else from infra.
[06:43] Lena: No more from ML.
[06:45] Priya: I'll follow up with security questions after we review the pack.
[06:49] Maya: Great — recap of next steps: send pricing + SOW + security pack by 3/6, schedule deep-dive 3/9, get traffic/profile from Sam by 3/5, benchmark window targeted 3/16.
[06:59] Sam: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:02] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

(Transcript ends — rough auto timestamps every ~30–60s; transcription includes minor recognition errors typical of automated tools.)
